definitions.gloss: to remake; to remodel; to redo; to reconstruct
definitions.explanation: To make something again from scratch, or to significantly alter something by remaking it in a different way. Used for both physical objects and abstract things like systems or plans.

examples.japanese: ドレスを{作|つく}り{替|か}えた。
{古|ふる}い{棚|たな}を{作|つく}り{替|か}えて{本棚|ほんだな}にした。
examples.english: I remodeled an old shelf and turned it into a bookcase.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}を{一|いち}から{作|つく}り{替|か}える{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to rebuild the system from scratch.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Ichidan verb (える ending: {作|つく}り{替|か}えない, {作|つく}り{替|か}えます). Transitive — takes a direct object marked with を. This is a compound verb combining {作|つく}る (to make) and {替|か}える (to change/replace).

USAGE:
{作|つく}り{替|か}える implies creating something new to replace the old version, not just minor modifications. It suggests a more fundamental remaking than {直|なお}す (to fix/repair).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一|いち}から{作|つく}り{替|か}える (to remake from scratch)
- {制度|せいど}を{作|つく}り{替|か}える (to overhaul a system)
- {間取|まど}りを{作|つく}り{替|か}える (to remodel the floor plan)
- {衣装|いしょう}を{作|つく}り{替|か}える (to remake a costume)
